text:
maria: Heads-up: noticed a p99 decode regression on canary correlated with structured-output function calls. Small requests are getting split into many micro-batches when the decoder emits a tool-call signature or stop-like separators.

raj: Any kernel churn metrics? That usually hints at kernel-selection thrash.

maria: Yes. Kernel picks spike whenever a batch is flushed for a tool boundary then resumed. Example from profiler:

```
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] batch=0x7f size=22 seq=0..21 kernel=KERNEL_OPT_A
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] batch=0x7f early_stop tool_sig->flush size=13 kernel=KERNEL_OPT_A
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] batch=0x80 size=2 seq=13..14 kernel=KERNEL_OPT_B
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] batch=0x81 size=1 seq=15 kernel=KERNEL_OPT_A
```

maria: Median batch size fell from ~20 to ~8 under structured-output traffic; tiny-batch tail rose and p99 decode latency jumped ~12%.

sasha: Sounds like stop-token detection is too aggressive for tool/structured output. Are we doing exact matching or suffix heuristics?

maria: Exact match today. Many structured fields include separators that the decoder treats as stop. Proposal: treat tool-invoke and structured-output stop events as "soft stops" so we can wait a brief coalescing window before flushing.

andy: Soft-stop window makes sense. Two knobs: token_grace (N tokens) and time_grace (M ms). Also consider nudging token_budget_target up for short-message traffic so kernel choice stabilizes.

maria: Draft config for canary A/B:

```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: "30"  # was 22
  stop_soft_grace_tokens: "3"
  stop_soft_grace_ms: "8"
  allow_coalesce_on_tool_sig: "true"
kv:
  kv_pin_ttl_ms: "750"  # was 250 to survive short tool handoffs
```

maria: Started an A/B perf run: /ci run perf/continuous-batcher/softstop-ab (id=4021). perf-bot: job queued.

perf-bot: Job queued: perf/continuous-batcher/softstop-ab (id=4021)

raj: Two other risks: 1) longer KV pin TTL increases mem footprint; monitor eviction rate. 2) Bumping token_budget_target may bias kernel pick towards longer-context kernels; watch tail p99 for big-requests.

sasha: Agreed. Instrument these: kernel_switch_count/min, small_batch_fraction (<=3 tokens), kv_pin_evictions/min, and a new metric soft_stop_coalesces/min. Add alert if mem usage > 85% on canary nodes.

maria: First 1h results: small_batch_fraction down 16% -> 6%, kernel_switch_count -40%, p99 decode latency improved ~9%, median steady. Cost impact: avg tokens/request +0.8% from soft padding.

andy: Nice. Any odd regressions on tail?

maria: One outlier: a multi-tool conversation with nested tool calls had a small spike in memory during the first 20s of the run. Likely KV pinning + concurrency. TTL tuned down to 600ms in the second wave. No stable failures.

sasha: Plan: roll to Dedicated staging for 24h smoke with telemetry dashboards: kernel_switch_count, soft_stop_coalesces, small_batch_fraction, kv_pin_evictions, and decode_p99. If stable, roll to production with a gradual ramp.

raj: Long-term: explore a learned coalescer that predicts whether a stop is final vs a structured-field seam. That could reduce false flushes without adding latency windows. Not necessary for the hotfix though.

maria: Filed INF-3287 tracker with the experiment artifacts and graphs: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3287. Assigning to sasha for staging rollout.

sasha: Will coordinate rollout and post the 24h graphs here. :rocket:
